title: The five aggregates are the burden, The bearer of the burden is the person. Taking up the burden is suffering in the world, Laying down…
content:
The five aggregates are the burden,
The bearer of the burden is the person.
Taking up the burden is suffering in the world,
Laying down the burden is happiness, free from suffering.
Having laid down the heavy burden,
One takes up no other burden.
Having pulled out craving, root and all,
One is free from hunger and thirst,
Fully extinguished, at peace.

title: Elder Māluṅkyaputta: Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost — If one attends to a pleasing perception, The mind feels infatuation, Gets stuck and remains. His…
content:
Elder Māluṅkyaputta:

Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from form —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Hearing a sound, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from sound —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Smelling an odor, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from odor —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Tasting a flavor, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from taste —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Feeling a touch, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from touch —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Cognizing a phenomenon, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from mind —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

title: Elder Uttara: “Nothing exists here that is permanent, No conditioned thing is everlasting. The aggregates arise and cease, They pass away in another existence. Knowing…
content:
Elder Uttara:
“Nothing exists here that is permanent,
No conditioned thing is everlasting.
The aggregates arise and cease,
They pass away in another existence.

Knowing this danger,
I do not desire existence.
Having abandoned all sensual desires,
I have realized the destruction of defilements.”

title: “He contemplates all forms, feelings, perceptions, formations, and consciousness as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as misery, as…
content: “He contemplates all forms, feelings, perceptions, formations, and consciousness as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as misery, as an affliction, as alien, as disintegrating, as empty, as not-self. He turns his mind away from these states and directs it towards the deathless element: ‘This is peaceful, this is sublime—namely, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all attachments, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’ If he is firm in this, he attains the destruction of the defilements. If he does not yet attain the destruction of the defilements, then by that same Dhamma-lust, Dhamma-delight, and by the destruction of the five lower fetters, he becomes one who is reborn spontaneously (in the Pure Abodes) and there attains final Nibbāna, never to return from that world.”

title: “Monks, here a clansman, abandoning sensual pleasures, goes forth from the household life into homelessness. But because of those sensual pleasures, or other sensual pleasures…
content: “Monks, here a clansman, abandoning sensual pleasures, goes forth from the household life into homelessness. But because of those sensual pleasures, or other sensual pleasures worse than those, he is destroyed, ruined, falls, lies prostrate. These five hindrances, monks, are obscurations, hindrances, coverings of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. What five? Sensual desire, monks, is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. Ill-will … sloth and torpor … restlessness and remorse … doubt, monks, is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. These five hindrances, monks, are obscurations, hindrances, coverings of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. The seven factors of enlightenment, monks, are not obscurations, not hindrances, not coverings of the mind; when developed and cultivated, they lead to the realization of the fruit of true knowledge and liberation. What seven? The mindfulness factor of enlightenment … The equanimity factor of enlightenment — these are not obscurations, not hindrances, not coverings of the mind; when developed and cultivated, they lead to the realization of the fruit of true knowledge and liberation.”

title: Elder Parāpariya: “Having abandoned the six sense-bases, With sense-doors well restrained, Having pulled out the root of evil, I have attained the destruction of defilements.”
content:
Elder Parāpariya:
“Having abandoned the six sense-bases,
With sense-doors well restrained,
Having pulled out the root of evil,
I have attained the destruction of defilements.”

title: “When, monks, a monk is not lustful regarding objects that can provoke lust, and his self is free from lust; is not hateful regarding objects…
content: “When, monks, a monk is not lustful regarding objects that can provoke lust, and his self is free from lust; is not hateful regarding objects that can provoke hatred, and his self is free from hatred; is not deluded regarding objects that can provoke delusion, and his self is free from delusion; is not infatuated regarding objects that can provoke infatuation, and his self is free from infatuation — then he has no fear, no trembling, no terror, does not fall into fear, and does not go by whatever ascetics may say.”

title: “For a person who lives heedlessly, Craving grows like a creeping vine. He leaps from life to life, Like a monkey seeking fruit in the…
content:
“For a person who lives heedlessly,
Craving grows like a creeping vine.
He leaps from life to life,
Like a monkey seeking fruit in the forest.”

“Whoever in this world is overcome by this wretched clinging,
His sorrows increase like well-watered birana grass.”

“Whoever in this world overcomes this wretched clinging,
Sorrows fall away from him like water drops from a lotus.”

title: “Poṭṭhapāda, I teach the Dhamma for the removal of gross personality view. If you practice accordingly, then defiling states are abandoned, pure states increase, and…
content: “Poṭṭhapāda, I teach the Dhamma for the removal of gross personality view. If you practice accordingly, then defiling states are abandoned, pure states increase, and in this very life, by direct knowledge, you realize and abide in full, vast wisdom. Poṭṭhapāda, you might think: ‘Defiling states will be abandoned, pure states will increase, and in this very life, by direct knowledge, one realizes and abides in full, vast wisdom — yet suffering still remains.’ Poṭṭhapāda, do not think thus. When defiling states are abandoned, pure states increase, and in this very life, by direct knowledge, one realizes and abides in full, vast wisdom — then gladness arises, joy, tranquility, mindfulness, clear comprehension, and a pleasant abiding arise.”

title: “Pleasant and delightful are sensual pleasures, In various forms both coarse and refined — Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure, Wander alone like…
content:
“Pleasant and delightful are sensual pleasures,
In various forms both coarse and refined —
Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure,
Wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”

“This is a boil, this is a calamity,
This is a disease, this is a dart —
Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure,
Wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”
